nodes.label: Application Layer Import Boundary
nodes.rationale: Interface layer imports only from application (services) and shared; services facades delegate to infrastructure, which interface never imports directly. Keeps the dependency arrow pointing inward (interface -> application -> infrastructure) so import-linter can enforce the boundary.

nodes.label: SEED_PROJECTS (bitch-stewie self-target preset)
nodes.rationale: Seeds the orchestrator's own repo as a Project so CC can self-rewrite it: 'CC edits here on a feature branch; merge the PR -> CI redeploys -> the running orchestrator restarts with the upgraded code.'

nodes.label: ECC plugin (scope change to user-wide)
nodes.rationale: Changed from scope:local (project mails) to scope:user on 2026-07-10 so its 67 agents/92 commands/277 skills load in every project; required a Claude Code restart to take effect. A caveat found by verification: ecc:deep-research needs firecrawl+exa MCPs which aren't connected, so the built-in deep-research skill is used instead for Chain C.

nodes.label: Chaining rules (§7)
nodes.rationale: Orchestrator stays clean: a workflow script/orchestrator must not read artifacts it spawns agents to produce, to avoid context overflow — it dispatches, collects structured results, and synthesizes.

nodes.label: Removed legacy user-level skills (§6)
nodes.rationale: ~90 skills in ~/.claude/skills/ were deleted on 2026-07-10 because they referenced agent types (sdd:*, sadd:*, superpowers:*) from plugins that were never installed, breaking at subagent spawn; the library now builds on ecc + built-ins instead.

nodes.label: OpenHands trial and removal
nodes.rationale: OpenHands was trialled on krisiserver and removed (2026-07-10) because it couldn't act as the Flow Manager: it can't spawn real Claude Code instances, whereas the bitch-stewie orchestrator does this through the CC SDK.
